title: Your Offer Fails This 5-Second Test
audience_problem: A beginner's offer sounds impressive but does not tell a buyer what they receive.
packaging_promise: Give a quick, explicitly non-scientific clarity exercise and a visible headline rewrite.
description:
Can someone understand your offer after a quick glance? This five-second exercise is a clarity heuristic, not a scientific cutoff. We rewrite a vague service headline into a specific fictional café offer.

An original BizNex framework with illustrative examples. Understanding an offer does not guarantee replies, clients or income. Only promise work you can actually deliver.

General marketing background: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/

The long Repair Lab episode builds the entire one-page offer.

sources.claim: The five-second exercise is an original clarity heuristic, not a validated benchmark. SBA supplies general target-market and sales-planning background only.

segments.title: The fuzzy headline
segments.text: Read this offer: I help businesses grow with creative solutions. After five seconds, what would you actually buy?

segments.title: A concrete headline
segments.text: Now this fictional example: One mobile friendly menu page for cafés, with clear prices and an enquiry button.

segments.title: Three clarity questions
segments.text: Ask someone: Who is it for? What do they get? What happens next? This is a clarity exercise, not science.

segments.title: Fix the first sentence
segments.text: If they cannot explain it, rewrite the headline before redesigning the whole website.
